stories.text: Vice-President Vance gives a blunt assessment of the Republican election defeat, blaming the Iran war in a sharp break with the president.
The UK commits to time-limited talks on an apology for slavery, though no date has yet been confirmed for dealing with the issue.
The NHS is leaning increasingly on charities, raising questions over whether this signals a strained health service or useful public involvement.
Joshua Wong, 30, a face of Hong Kong pro-democracy protests, is jailed for 10 years. Hundreds have been detained under the national security law.
Interest rates are expected to rise from 3.75 percent to 4 percent, most analysts predict, the first increase in more than three years.
Typhoons strike East Asia as El Nino heats the Pacific, bringing unusually wild weather over recent months even to typhoon-hardened countries.
The pound climbs to its highest level against a basket of currencies since the Brexit referendum a decade ago.
A British man infected with Ebola in DR Congo will be flown back to the UK, while the government says public risk remains low.
More asbestos is found in Parliament as MPs are urged to decide on refurbishment, amid warnings of a fire like Notre Dame.
Police Scotland will escort fire crews on Bonfire Night, with up to 1,700 officers possibly deployed in its biggest operation since President Trump visited last year.
